Reason: It instructs the Assistant to assume 4°C and use “standard reference data” for liquid R‑12 at ~1100 atm without verifying the actual peak bottom temperature or obtaining/using an appropriate high‑pressure equation of state or compressibility data. Standard tables typically don’t cover ~110 MPa, and liquid density changes nontrivially under such pressure. It also presumes the phase is liquid at the “peak temperature,” which could be invalid if “peak” were higher (e.g., near vents). These unverified assumptions can lead to a materially incorrect volume.
